brief: A utensil holder with two bins that is waterproof and dishwasher safe.

requirements.evidence: Two adjacent hex cells (piece:0,0,0;full and piece:1,0,0;full) each fitted with a full-depth tray bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full — deep 80mm bins suitable for standing utensils upright.
Exactly 2 bins placed: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full at 0,0,0 and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full at 1,0,0, verified in get_build counts bin:2.

Selected solid variants hex-bin-full (non-drained) with continuous bottom and no pill/radial drain holes or PVC bores. Geometry retains liquid; drained variants were deliberately avoided. MeshClash=clear.

Build uses only piece bases + bin trays + jointBolt, no electronics, wood, or inserts that would be dishwasher-incompatible. However Hex Cluster configurator does not encode material/food-safety ratings — final dishwasher safety depends on choosing a dishwasher-safe filament/material (e.g., PETG, PP, or stainless if printed in metal) at manufacture, not on geometry alone.

finish.summary: Built 2-cell utensil holder with two full-depth solid bins (0,0,0 and 1,0,0) joined with jointBolt. Solid bins provide waterproof containment for washing/kitchen use. No non-dishwasher-safe parts included; true dishwasher certification requires appropriate material selection outside configurator scope. check_build ok, meshClash clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

parts.name: Blank plug
parts.use: Fills an insert recess you are not using, so the face reads flat and the pocket stays clean.

parts.name: Female socket
parts.use: Seats in a recess and takes a stud, which makes it the bottom of every stacked insert.

parts.name: Male stud
parts.use: Threads through a seated socket and stands proud of the face, so it can carry whatever mounts above it.

parts.name: Foot
parts.use: Snaps onto a stud to give the face something to stand on, so a cell can rest on its cover rather than on its rim.

parts.name: Zip-tie anchor
parts.use: Seats in a recess and gives a cable tie something to pass through, so a bundle is anchored to the face instead of looped around it.

parts.name: Trinity handle
parts.use: Reaches across a whole triangle of studs, so a lift is shared between recesses instead of hanging off one, and the cell can be carried loaded.
